text: Identify the exact result or quote, its source and the qualifying context. Preserve meaning, units, time window and attribution; do not turn an observation into a guarantee. Quote text stays verbatim unless an explicitly marked excerpt preserves the meaning. A logo alone does not substantiate a customer relationship.

Bind every proof and attribution copy block to evidence IDs … never a fabricated URL. The schema checks joins; it cannot verify the truth of a quote. Without usable proof, choose type-led positioning and name what was unavailable.

Make the proof the focal element with native text; give context and attribution enough space to be read. Use authentic customer logos only when authorized by the source context. Cards, quote marks and buttons are optional.
Review evidence fidelity and visible qualification before judging polish. If the footnote is essential to understanding the claim, it cannot be decorative microtype.

Read the complete relevant story, not only its hero metric … Distinguish the customer's report, the vendor's interpretation and a measured experiment. A sequence of events does not establish that the product caused everything that happened afterward.

Write the headline around the change; support supplies the mechanism and context. Preserve units, timeframe, affected team and qualifying language … Quotes remain exact or faithful marked excerpts; paraphrases have no quotation marks.

Inspect the advertiser's actual customer-story ads and the customer's approved source assets … Keep campaign treatment separate from customer evidence … When campaign pixels are unavailable, record that limitation.
Three shapes: Outcome with a visible bridge; The changed situation; Editorial excerpt. Not mandatory three-card timelines … select a narrower slice or record that a multi-page format is needed.
Generated art may illustrate a concept; it cannot depict a fabricated customer event, employee, quotation, dashboard result or endorsement as real evidence.

Use a read-the-story action when the destination is the case study; do not promise that viewers will achieve the same result … Review for a truthful challenge-to-action-to-result link … If no approved customer evidence is usable, switch to supported product positioning and report the missing story.
A logo wall is not a customer story, and an account targeted by an ABM campaign must not be portrayed as an existing customer.

Confirm the relationship, named organization, team or person, product used and supported result. Keep a team-level experience at that scope … An available logo file is not evidence of endorsement or consent to an invented joint announcement.

When quoting, preserve the approved words and attribution; do not manufacture first-person language from a third-person case study. Use the advertiser's editorial voice to frame the story, and preserve the customer's distinct voice where sourced.
Three compositions: Person and practice (no synthetic stand-in for that person); Customer world; Editorial co-brand feature.

Let inspected original customer campaigns establish the advertiser/customer hierarchy and CTA treatment. Preserve supplied lockups, clear space and identity colors … Vary the story angle or authentic scene deliberately without inventing another relationship.

Keep each logo, portrait, product image and artwork as an independent layer. Do not generate a combined customer/advertiser logo or bake native attribution into the photograph. No decorative growth curve should imply customer performance.
Without a confirmed relationship, do not create the requested spotlight. Explain the missing evidence and use an anonymous supported scenario only when the user allows that alternate purpose.
Probe "Feature our customer in an ad" with a narrative-only source and again with only a logo; the first can work, the second cannot establish the story.
